name: Ofélia Mwangi-Strandqvist
description: Ofélia Mwangi-Strandqvist is the most canonized director of the flat-screen revival movement, a Kenyan-Swedish filmmaker from the Shelf who spent forty years refusing every neural-feed offer and every corporate license application. Her films are shot on recovered optical cameras and distributed exclusively on physical media — pressed discs, hand-labeled, passed between viewers in Tier 1 and 2 communities. Her debut feature, *The Patience of Concrete*, documented a single Shelf building over the course of three years and was never legally released; it circulated for a decade before anyone admitted to having seen it.
cultural_impact: Mwangi-Strandqvist almost single-handedly legitimized flat-screen as a political medium rather than a poverty medium, and her aesthetic influenced a generation of underground directors who call themselves the 'Concrete School.'
story_hooks: A pressed disc of her banned 2201 film surfaces at a dead drop and contains footage of something that was never meant to be filmed — a corporate operation caught incidentally in the background.
Mwangi-Strandqvist is dying and wants to transfer her archive to someone trustworthy before Axiom can seize it — but her only copy is inside a building about to be demolished.
A young director claims to have found footage she shot but never released, depicting events that powerful people insist never happened.
